patient_selection.evidence: Abnormal volumes were selected from the larger pool to include a broad variety of abnormal conditions, including acute and chronic ischemia, hemorrhage, intra- and extra-axial masses
patient_selection.rationale: The 69 reader-study volumes were purposively enriched for abnormality from a larger retrospective test set rather than sampled consecutively or at random.

index_test.evidence: Two neuroradiologists with 20 (Y.W.L.) and 5 (E.L.) years of experience independently reviewed ground truth reconstruction and deep learning reconstructions at all accelerations.
index_test.rationale: Readers graded the accelerated reconstructions in a double-stimulus presentation alongside the identified fully sampled ground truth, so index-test interpretation was not blinded to the reference; quality thresholds were, however, pre-specified.

reference_standard.evidence: although undersampling was performed retrospectively, it was performed on actual raw, multireceiver channel k-space data provided in the fastMRI dataset, which was obtained directly from MRI scanners
reference_standard.rationale: The reference was the fully sampled reconstruction from genuine multi-coil raw k-space, an appropriate ground truth for judging what accelerated reconstruction preserves.

flow_timing.evidence: For radiologist evaluation, we reviewed a subgroup of 69 volumes (29 T2-weighted, 20 T2 FLAIR, and 20 T1-weighted examinations) from the test set with a balance of normal and abnormal cases
flow_timing.rationale: Index and reference images derive from the same raw k-space (zero interval) and all 69 volumes (29/20/20) are accounted for in the reported results tables.

app_patient_selection.evidence: The dataset includes raw k-space data from 6405 fully sampled clinical brain MR images (including normal and abnormal clinical studies) obtained using standard 2D imaging sequences
app_patient_selection.rationale: Routine clinical brain MRI containing both normal and a wide range of abnormal studies matches the review population.

app_index_test.evidence: we enlarged and adapted the End-to-End Variational Network (12) to reconstruct standard clinical two-dimensional (2D) spin-echo brain MR images
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is a deep-learning reconstruction of undersampled brain MRI evaluated across acceleration factors, exactly the technology of interest.

app_reference_standard.evidence: defined as image quality undifferentiable from state-of-the-art routine clinical diagnostic imaging currently obtained at an academic tertiary care center based on subspecialist neuroradiology review
app_reference_standard.rationale: The fully sampled acquisition plus subspecialist neuroradiologist review is the reference standard the review question presumes.

patient_selection.evidence: In this retrospective study, MRA images of 40 patients (21 males and 19 females; mean age, 65.8 ± 13.2 years) were reconstructed with and without the DLR technique
patient_selection.rationale: Only abstract text is available; no consecutive or random sampling rule, inclusion criteria, or exclusions are described for the 40 retrospective cases.

index_test.evidence: Two experienced radiologists evaluated the depiction of structures (the right internal carotid artery, right ophthalmic artery, basilar artery, and right superior cerebellar artery), artifacts, subjective noise and overall image quality
index_test.rationale: No statement that the two radiologists were blinded to whether an image was the DLR or non-DLR reconstruction, and no pre-specified thresholds are reported.

reference_standard.evidence: reconstructed with and without the DLR technique (DLR image and non-DLR image, respectively)
reference_standard.rationale: The comparator is simply the non-DLR reconstruction of the same data; no independent ground truth or blinded reference reading is described.

flow_timing.evidence: Scores were compared in the quantitative and qualitative image analyses between the DLR and non-DLR images using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
flow_timing.rationale: Paired within-subject analysis of two reconstructions of the same acquisition implies a zero interval and that all 40 patients contributed to both arms.

app_patient_selection.evidence: MRA images of 40 patients (21 males and 19 females; mean age, 65.8 ± 13.2 years) were reconstructed with and without the DLR technique
app_patient_selection.rationale: Adult patients undergoing clinical intracranial MR angiography are within the brain MRI population of interest.

app_index_test.evidence: The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether deep learning reconstruction (DLR) improves the image quality of intracranial magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) at 1.5 T.
app_index_test.rationale: A vendor deep-learning reconstruction applied to intracranial MR imaging is the class of index test the review concerns.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Quantitative image analysis was performed by placing regions of interest on the basilar artery and cerebrospinal fluid in the prepontine cistern.
app_reference_standard.rationale: Outcomes are SNR/CNR and subjective quality surrogates against the non-DLR image; no diagnostic ground truth is defined, so the match to preservation of diagnostic content is uncertain.

patient_selection.evidence: We apply the technique to the 2016 QSM Challenge and in 10 glioblastoma multiforme datasets.
patient_selection.rationale: Available text (abstract and introduction only) gives no sampling frame, inclusion criteria, or selection rule for the 10 glioblastoma datasets.

index_test.evidence: Reconstructions on glioblastoma data were analyzed using ranked and semiquantitative image grading by three neuroradiologist observers to assess image quality (IQ) and sharpness (IS).
index_test.rationale: No information on whether the three observers were blinded to which reconstruction algorithm produced each map, nor on pre-specified grading thresholds.

reference_standard.evidence: We compared its performance with four published QSM techniques and a multi-orientation QSM method.
reference_standard.rationale: A multi-orientation (COSMOS) reference was available only for the challenge data; the clinical glioblastoma grading was relative ranking against other algorithms with no independent ground truth described.

flow_timing.rationale: The accessible text does not report how many cases each observer graded, whether any were excluded, or the flow of datasets through the analyses.

app_patient_selection.evidence: We apply the technique to the 2016 QSM Challenge and in 10 glioblastoma multiforme datasets.
app_patient_selection.rationale: Patients with intracranial pathology undergoing brain MRI fall within the review population, albeit a small and narrow sample.

app_index_test.evidence: We developed PnP QSM using alternating direction method of multiplier framework and applied collaborative filtering denoisers.
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is a regularized iterative QSM reconstruction with patch-based denoisers rather than an accelerated or deep-learning reconstruction, so its fit to the review question is uncertain.

app_reference_standard.evidence: We analyzed magnetic susceptibility accuracy using brain region-of-interest measurements, and image quality using global error metrics.
app_reference_standard.rationale: Reference outcomes are susceptibility accuracy and global error metrics rather than a fully sampled acquisition or expert diagnostic reading of preserved clinical content.

patient_selection.evidence: Ninety-seven patients who underwent routine brain MR imaging examination between August 2021 and January 2022 in the inpatient and emergency department settings were included in this study.
patient_selection.rationale: A defined single-centre time window is given but the study never states that enrolment was consecutive or random, and no inclusion or exclusion rule is described.

index_test.evidence: Two neuroradiologists (M.L. and J.F. with 3 and 5 years of experience, respectively) performed independent blinded reviews of unlabeled MPRAGE images without and with SAMER motion correction.
index_test.rationale: Readers were blinded to reconstruction type, images were unlabeled and independently reviewed, and a previously established 5-point motion scale was used.

reference_standard.evidence: The order of the study and the type of study (baseline-versus-SAMER motion-corrected images) were randomized by A.T. for the reviewing neuroradiologists.
reference_standard.rationale: The standard non-motion-corrected reconstruction was graded blind and in randomized order by the same neuroradiologists, with a third blinded senior reader adjudicating discrepancies.

flow_timing.evidence: The same 2 neuroradiologists (M.L. and J.F.) independently reviewed 79 of 97 cases with pathology in a blinded fashion; 18 cases did not have visible pathology on MPRAGE images.
flow_timing.rationale: Both reconstructions come from the same raw k-space (zero interval), all 97 cases appear in the motion-grade analysis, and the 18 cases omitted from the head-to-head substudy are explained.

app_patient_selection.evidence: Ninety-seven patients who underwent MR imaging in the inpatient and emergency department settings were included in the study.
app_patient_selection.rationale: Unselected clinical inpatient and emergency brain MRI patients are directly relevant to whether an advanced reconstruction is safe in routine practice.

app_index_test.evidence: SAMER motion correction was retrospectively applied to an accelerated T1-weighted MPRAGE sequence that was included in brain MR imaging examinations performed with and without contrast.
app_index_test.rationale: An advanced model-based reconstruction applied to an R=4 accelerated brain acquisition matches the review's index-test concept.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Two blinded neuroradiologists graded images with and without SAMER motion correction on a 5-tier motion severity scale (none = 1, minimal = 2, mild = 3, moderate = 4, severe = 5).
app_reference_standard.rationale: The conventional reconstruction of the same acquisition, read by expert neuroradiologists with an explicit diagnostic/nondiagnostic cut-off, is the intended standard-of-care reference.

patient_selection.evidence: consisting of 20 cases (4 FLAIR, 5 T1-weighted, and 11 T2-weighted volumes) with abnormalities (clinical dataset)
patient_selection.rationale: The reader cohort was a purposively chosen subset of abnormal cases carried over from a prior study, not a consecutive or random sample of the test set.

index_test.evidence: All radiologists had knowledge of the ground-truth, but were blinded to the particular reconstruction model and performed their reviews independently.
index_test.rationale: Reconstruction model identity was masked, but readers scored each accelerated reconstruction while knowingly viewing the labelled fully sampled ground truth, so interpretation was not blinded to the reference.

reference_standard.evidence: The fastMRI dataset includes both the raw k-space data and ground-truth MRI images presented in this work.
reference_standard.rationale: The fully sampled reconstruction from raw multi-coil k-space is an appropriate reference for judging preserved image content.

flow_timing.evidence: Each radiologist was assigned the ground-truth fully-sampled image and two undersampled reconstructions: one with the FI VarNet (12 feature-12 image cascades)
flow_timing.rationale: Retrospective undersampling of the same raw data gives a zero interval, and all three readers scored all 20 cases (reported as x/20 for every reader).

app_patient_selection.evidence: The abnormalities included postsurgical complications, vascular-related conditions, masses and tumors, and fluid-related conditions.
app_patient_selection.rationale: Clinical brain MRI containing a spread of real pathology is the population in which loss of diagnostic content matters.

app_index_test.evidence: Reconstructions were evaluated on the fastMRI dataset using standard metrics and clinical scoring by three neuroradiologists.
app_index_test.rationale: Deep-learning reconstruction of 4x to 8x Cartesian undersampled brain MRI, scored by neuroradiologists, is precisely the index test of interest.

app_reference_standard.evidence: three Likert-like grading scales were used to assess artifacts, sharpness, and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), in comparison to the ground-truth
app_reference_standard.rationale: Expert grading explicitly referenced to the fully sampled ground truth matches the review's reference standard.

patient_selection.evidence: The scans were chosen to encompass a wide range of artifacts, but not considering any disease status.
patient_selection.rationale: Scans were purposively selected to span the artifact spectrum rather than sampled consecutively or randomly, which inflates the quality range on which the index was trained and tested.

index_test.evidence: The dotted line in the plot shows the point corresponding to a 99% sensitivity and 79% specificity, and a QEI value of 0.53.
index_test.rationale: The QEI cut-off of 0.53 was derived post hoc from the same ROC analysis and its parameters were fitted to the same expert ratings, so the threshold was not pre-specified (leave-one-out cross-validation only partly mitigates this).

reference_standard.evidence: Two neuroradiologists (RW with 23 years of experience and SAN with 12 years of experience in interpreting ASL images) rated the 101 CBF maps shown in Table 1 based on visual inspection.
reference_standard.rationale: Independent visual ratings by two highly experienced neuroradiologists, made before the automated index existed, are an acceptable reference read independent of the index test (inter-rater R = 0.81).

flow_timing.evidence: We discarded the data of two subjects, one for having a single control-label pair for which the computation of ASL-MC QI was not possible
flow_timing.rationale: Index and reference are computed on the identical CBF maps (zero interval) and the only exclusions are enumerated with explicit reasons.

app_patient_selection.evidence: Data from N = 221 adults, including patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease, and traumatic brain injury.
app_patient_selection.rationale: Adults undergoing brain MRI across several neurological conditions fall within the review population.

app_index_test.evidence: To develop an automated and objective quality evaluation index (QEI) for ASL CBF maps.
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is an automated image-quality metric for ASL perfusion maps, not an accelerated or deep-learning reconstruction, so it does not address whether accelerated reconstruction preserves diagnostic content.

app_reference_standard.evidence: The maps were rated based on the level of image artifacts relative to plausible CBF information on a scale between 1 and 4
app_reference_standard.rationale: Expert visual ratings act as ground truth, but the target condition is ASL map quality rather than preserved diagnostic content relative to a fully sampled or conventional acquisition.
